title: Injuids
capsule: The Injuids (Āl-e Inju) were an Iranian dynasty of Persian origin who governed Fars, Khuzestan, and Isfahan in the mid-fourteenth century, originating as superintendents of the Ilkhanate's royal estates (injü, 'crown property'). After the death of the last Ilkhan Abu Sa'id in 1335, the Injuid governor Shaikh Abu Ishaq asserted full independence and made Shiraz a celebrated centre of manuscript illustration, commissioning the Shahnama and Divan copies that defined the Injuid artistic style—vivid colour fields, dynamic compositions, and distinctive yellow-background mountain landscapes. Abu Ishaq was captured by the rival Muzaffarid dynasty and executed in Shiraz in 1357, ending Injuid rule.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Injuids' urban holdings in Shiraz and Isfahan are well-attested through Persian chronicles and colophons; their rural and provincial reach fluctuated and is less precisely mapped.
